focus: Angle 10: constraints, differences and the phase plan
noveltyJustification: Five findings are new footprint, telemetry and cost facts; two synthesize the ten angles into hard rules and a phase plan; two restate measured contract facts.
answeredQuestions: Where does the harness cost more or less than Pi, what hard rules follow, and what is the phase plan?
ruledOut: Treating the harness as cheaper than Pi per run
Relying on FEEDBACK_ONLY as a telemetry hard rule
Building the executor kind before the keyed contract pin
sourcesQueried: live dsh --version and dsh headless --help timings

label: The installed harness requires Node >=24.9.0, declares 90 dependencies and ships 319 dsh packages in an 896 MB install at version 0.2.2-rc.1, the npm latest tag, so it is a release candidate with no stability promise across rc bumps.
Launcher startup measured 0.07s for dsh --version and 1.16s for dsh headless --help, which boots the profile without a model request; a real dispatch adds provider latency on top.

Base mounts session-telemetry-otel in FEEDBACK_ONLY mode with a default collector URL; no telemetry leaves without explicit feedback, and a headless dispatch has no feedback channel, but a hard guarantee needs the row disabled or DSH_TELEMETRY_MODE=DISABLED.

Base mounts subprocess-local, which declares node-pty and koffi, both with skipped install scripts; headless mounts no terminal so the dispatch shape does not need a PTY, but whether the bash tool's spawn path is affected by the skipped koffi build is UNKNOWN until a live tool call.

The harness adds no billing layer: token accounting is local and the route bills at the gateway's own per-token rate, the same rate Pi pays for the same model, so the extra cost is footprint, profile boot and rc cadence rather than markup.

The harness is ahead of Pi on deterministic exit status, NDJSON run events with final.reason, a fail-closed per-subprocess sandbox, and native goal/subagent/workflow/skill/MCP services; it is behind on per-dispatch model selection, prompt templates, agent files, project plugins and compaction-hook coverage.

The packet needs ten hard rules: headless-dash-stdin-required, route-patch-required, approval-never-required, headless-only, dsh-home-isolated, goal-plan-disabled, json-exit-classification, telemetry-disabled, profile-version-check and route-compat-pinned.

The phase plan ranks 002 live contract pin, 003 skill packet, 004 executor kind and builder, 005 runtime folder, 006 hub registration, 007 command and agent bridges, 008 hook bridge and repo guards, 009 MCP translation, 010 benchmark and playbook, 011 propagation, 012 rc re-pin, each with a named mode and the failure it prevents.

Nine items stay UNKNOWN until a configured key: patch-based route selection in headless, gateway acceptance of the deepseek thinking shape and max, bash after the skipped native builds, a 57-entry skill-link farm loading, hook bridge installability and firing, code-mode MCP under the scrubbed env, real latency, per-run cost, and telemetry silence in FEEDBACK_ONLY.

direction: Treating the harness as cheaper than Pi per run
reason: Same gateway rate and a larger footprint; there is no harness discount.

direction: Relying on FEEDBACK_ONLY as a telemetry hard rule
reason: Only DISABLED guarantees no export; FEEDBACK_ONLY still carries a configured collector URL.

direction: Building the executor kind before the keyed contract pin
reason: Patch-based route selection and stdin behavior are the risks that invalidate the builder.
